subject: Genetics
title: Precision Epigenetics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Precision Epigenetics.

hook.text: Current epigenetic drugs hit every gene. What if we could target one specific gene's marks? CRISPR makes it possible.

buildup.text: Dead Cas9 (dCas9) can't cut DNA—but it can carry epigenetic enzymes to a precise location.

discovery.text: Scientists fused dCas9 to methylation enzymes and silenced specific genes without changing the DNA.

twist.text: Unlike gene editing, epigenetic editing is reversible. Turn a gene off today, reactivate it tomorrow.

climax.text: Precision epigenetics could treat diseases by adjusting gene activity like a dimmer switch—a tunable dial, not a blunt tool.

punchline.text: Don't cut the gene. Just turn the volume knob.

quiz.question: What does dCas9 do in precision epigenetics?
options: Delivers epigenetic enzymes to specific genes
